newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African industrial shares seen buoyant next week.
newsitem.headline: S.African industrial shares seen buoyant next week.

text.p: South African industrial shares were seen firm next week on a host of positive factors born this week, dealers and portfolio managers said on Friday.
Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals' comments that he anticipated a "very stable" rand in 1997 which could decline by less than inflation differentials were well received offshore.

The December trade surplus figure also beat eforecasts, coming in at 2.04 billion rand compared to 378 million surplus in November and bringing the year surplus to 10.577 billion rand against 4.884 billion in 1995.
The rand also strengthened during the week and dealers said it would encourage foreign investors to look at the local market which was "grossly" undervalued relative to overseas markets.

"The comments from the governor of the Reserve Bank were positive, we had good statistics on the trade account, long rates eased. The story is upbeat. We have had pent-up demand for equities and the outlook is positive in the short-term," an asset manager who declined to be identified said.
U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments on the U.S. economy were perceived as non-inflationery which could boost U.S. stocks with spin-offs for local shares, dealers said.
But Wall Street weakened on Wednesday and fell 94.28 points to 6,755.75 points on Thursday night in heavy volumes.
Dealers said if Wall Street eased overnight on Friday -- and indications were it would be weak -- institutions could return to the local market at lower levels later next week.

"The market will be relatively cautious. If we see a correction on the Dow overnight, we could see a firmer market towards the end of the week," Dominick Rey, a senior dealer at Investec Fergusson Bros told Reuters.
"If Wall Street consolidates around these levels. There is no reason for our market not to rise. We saw a good correction in the past two days," a director at a local brokerage said.
The gold price suffered this week, breaking below the psychologically important $350 bid per ounce.
The rally in the yellow metal on Thursday was seen short-lived as it was based on short-covering, dealers said.
"We had some short covering on golds last night. The market does not respond massively to such shortcovering. It is not sustainable. There is still weakness on the gold price," one dealer said.
Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd December quarter mining results are due on Monday and dealers said they expected good results based on the group's track record.
Anglovaal's results are due on Tuesday.
December CPI and preliminary money supply figures are due from Monday. Economists polled by Reuters forecast CPI up to 9.6 percent year-on-year from 9.2 percent in November.
The consensus forecast was for M3 year-on-year growth of 14.3 percent from 15.32 in November while private credit is seen expanding 16.3 percent against 17.10 percent.
